stories.title: Trump Announces ‘Biggest Oil Deal In World History’
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump announced on Friday that the United States has reached an agreement with Venezuela to secure majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves. The president described the arrangement as the "biggest oil deal in world history" and a significant boost to U.S. energy security.

Trump stated that the transaction was achieved at no cost to the American taxpayer, following his administration's removal of former Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro earlier this year. He suggested the deal could serve as a long-term solution to rising gas prices for consumers.

Venezuela’s interim president characterized the unusual agreement as a vital step toward reviving her country's economy. The announcement marks a major shift in U.S.-Venezuelan relations and energy policy.

stories.title: At March on Washington, an urgent plea for black voters to turn out in the midterm elections
stories.summary:
Civil rights groups and Democratic lawmakers gathered on the National Mall Friday for a commemorative March on Washington. The event honored Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s 1963 speech on voting rights and jobs while issuing an urgent plea for Black voter turnout in upcoming midterm elections.

Protesters began at the steps of the Lincoln Memorial, focusing their attention on racial justice and the legacy of the civil rights movement. The demonstration took place against a backdrop of recent changes to voting laws and redistricting measures that critics have condemned as detrimental to Black Americans.

stories.title: Mamdani Takes Aim At Hindu Group Over ‘Exclusionary Vision’
stories.summary:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has stated he will not support an upcoming event in Manhattan featuring Mohan Bhagwat. The gathering is scheduled to include a speech by the head of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), which is described as the ideological parent organization of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

Mamdani, who identifies as Muslim, criticized the group for what he termed an “exclusionary vision.” His remarks come amid broader concerns regarding Hindu nationalism in the United States. Human rights groups have also organized protests against Bhagwat’s visit to New York, highlighting tensions surrounding his presence and the political affiliations of the RSS.

stories.title: Nashville airport could be renamed in honor of Dolly Parton
stories.summary:
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has proposed renaming Nashville International Airport in honor of country music icon Dolly Parton. The announcement comes days after the legendary singer died at age 80 following a brief battle with cancer.

Lee described the move as a lasting tribute to Parton’s indelible legacy and her influence on generations across Tennessee and the world. He stated that he consulted with Parton’s team regarding the proposal before making it public.

The initiative follows a petition that gathered over 155,000 signatures supporting the change. The renaming would honor one of the state’s most famous cultural figures at its largest transportation hub.

stories.title: Controversial plans for a Daniel Andrews sculpture officially scrapped by Victorian government
stories.summary:
The Victorian government has officially cancelled plans to erect a statue of former Premier Daniel Andrews. The decision was made by current Premier Ben Carroll's administration.

The proposed sculpture was intended for installation outside Melbourne's Treasury Place. It had attracted significant controversy prior to its cancellation.

Critics, including the Liberal opposition, heavily criticized the project due to its cost. The estimated price tag for the statue was $134,000.

stories.title: Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic was unlawful, US judge rules
stories.summary:
A US federal judge ruled on Thursday that the Pentagon’s designation of Anthropic as a supply chain risk was unlawful. The court found that the Trump administration broke the law by targeting the AI firm for refusing to comply with defense department demands.

The ruling marks a significant legal victory for Anthropic, which argued that the blacklist could cost billions in lost business and reputational harm. The judge stated that an empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish or retaliate against government contractors.

This decision comes as a second lawsuit between Anthropic and the Pentagon continues in Washington. The verdict highlights ongoing tensions between federal agencies and private AI developers regarding compliance with defense sector requirements.

stories.title: Nicola Coughlan and Matt Lucas among stars backing campaign against AI voice cloning
stories.summary:
A group of prominent British actors has launched a campaign to oppose the use of artificial intelligence for voice cloning. The initiative, titled Save Our Voices Now, seeks to prevent AI technology from replicating real people's voices without consent.

The campaign is backed by well-known figures including Nicola Coughlan, Matt Lucas, and Hugh Bonneville. Other supporters include Luke Evans, Jen Brister, Siobhán McSweeney, and Pearl Mackie.

Approximately 80 individuals have signed an open letter addressed to Andy Burnham. The signatories are calling for new legislation that would protect voice ownership rights.

stories.title: Rwanda-Backed Rebels Enter Congo's Safe-Haven City
stories.summary:
Rwandan-backed rebels have entered Goma, a city in the Democratic Republic of Congo that had previously served as a safe haven for displaced residents.

Local witnesses reported hearing gunfire and shelling after rebel forces overran Congolese troops defending the area.

The United Nations estimates that more than one million displaced people are currently sheltering within the city, highlighting the severe humanitarian implications of the conflict.

stories.title: Palestinians Stream Back to Northern Gaza on Foot
stories.summary:
Palestinian residents have begun returning to northern Gaza on foot following a recent breakthrough in hostage release negotiations. Israel permitted displaced civilians to cross into the area after a military zone that had bisected the enclave was opened.

The movement marks a significant shift from previous restrictions, allowing families to return to their homes in the north. This development follows the resolution of a deadlock regarding the exchange of hostages held by Hamas.
